### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `3046b9a222071f76f0eaa8f896bb10eb` · 2026-09-23T22:34:06Z

> Owner decision needed on question 166 (docs/QUESTIONS.md): the one-slice wakeup promise versus the single stride queue (ASTRA D3). K5 is blocked on this; G1 cannot close without it.
> 
> THE GAP. Answer 103 (archive 2026-09-22) replaced the `first` flag with one stride queue for every budget and stated as its cost: "a driver woken by an interrupt re-enters at the minimum pass, so it runs within about one SLICE". KERNEL-SPEC R12, RESOURCES.md (Scheduling, Attack tests) and BUILD-PLAN WP-K5 acceptance all repeat that as a bound. It does not follow from the specified mechanism. R12 wakes at max(own pass, current minimum) and says nothing about ties or when preemption happens. A woken driver therefore waits for the remainder of the running slice plus one full SLICE for every runnable budget ranked ahead of it at an equal pass, and it keeps any larger pass it retained. No unconditional next-turn bound exists, and a large weight does not create one. Nothing has been measured. Either the claim is weakened or the scheduler is changed; an editor may not choose.
> 
> RECOMMENDATION (A): keep answer 103's mechanism, withdraw the universal one-slice claim, replace it with a specified tie rule and a measured target.
> - KERNEL-SPEC R12: delete the sentence "Because a waking budget re-enters at the current minimum pass, a driver woken by an interrupt runs within about one SLICE" and the open-qualification paragraph. Add: a waking budget is ranked ahead of already-queued budgets with an equal pass (deterministic tie handling, wake-first); preemption happens at slice end or at a deadline, never on wake alone; wakeup is prompt but not bounded, and no deadline follows from weight. Single queue, actual-runtime charging and the max wake rule are unchanged.
> - RESOURCES.md: remove the two open-166 paragraphs and the "Unresolved latency claim" bullet; state the wake rule as prompt-not-bounded with the tie rule; replace the attack-test bullet "a driver woken by an interrupt runs within about one SLICE while user budgets spin" with a measured responsiveness target under a named workload (N spinning user budgets at manifest user weight, one driver and the steward at manifest weights) that records weights, runnable budgets, prior passes, wake latency and lease-termination latency. Share, fairness and human-control text stay.
> - BUILD-PLAN WP-K5: replace the bold one-SLICE acceptance bullet with: deterministic tie handling implemented and tested; real-boot acceptance under the named workload reports the measured wake and lease-termination latencies with the recorded inputs; WP-K5 proposes the numeric target with its evidence and a package reviewer accepts it. Remove the design-gate line. Answer 103's "stated cost" wording is superseded by the new entry; TENETS' reference to open 166 is removed editorially.
> - Why: it preserves the accepted no-priority design, makes the guarantee honest and testable, and costs nothing in mechanism. Residual: human control (TENETS guarantee 3) then rests on a measured steward latency, not a proven bound.
> 
> ALTERNATIVE (B): keep a hard "within one SLICE" requirement and change the scheduler to establish it.
> - KERNEL-SPEC R12 gains a wake rule that guarantees the next turn (for example: a budget woken by an interrupt, or any budget above a weight threshold, is placed at the queue head with a rate limit per period), plus an explicit rule against sleeping to gain priority.
> - RESOURCES.md states the load assumptions under which the bound holds and the proof sketch; the attack-test bullet stays as a bound.
> - WP-K5 acceptance keeps the one-SLICE bullet and adds attack cases for sleep-wake gaming and starvation by several head-jumping budgets; a defensive review of the rule precedes implementation.
> - Cost: this reintroduces a form of the priority tier answer 103 removed, needs a new proof under stated assumptions, and delays K5 by that design and review.
> 
> MINOR VARIANT (A without a measured target): retain the qualification and let K5 ship with no latency claim at all. Not recommended: the steward's responsiveness underwrites lease termination, so some recorded evidence is needed.
> 
> Please answer A, B, or a variation with any change you want to the tie rule, the workload or the numeric target. Only your reply authorizes the edits; I will then record the decision in ANSWERS.md as a revision of 103, apply it to R12, RESOURCES.md and WP-K5, and return the thread to the orchestrator with decision references.
